>Except for [large breed] they are basically one size fits all

That's not entirely true. Cats are bred for different personalities, just like dogs were originally bred for different purposes (retrieving, ratting, companionship) and recently certain cat breeds are also bred for level of allergen production. [Large breed] are only one example of purebred cats. One of the most well-known, but not fundamentally bred differently than any other breed such as a [fluffy breed], [vocal breed], [athletic breed] or [hypoallergenic breed]. [Large breed] are bred to be large, intelligent and very independent. [Vocal breed] are talkers and can be quite aloof. [Athletic breed] are extremely athletic and tend to take to harnesses better than most. [Hypoallergenic breed] are good for those with allergies. [Fluffy breed] are lap cats which are great for smaller spaces and older people. You get the idea.

Personally, I've lived with [fluffy breed] (and now an [exotic breed]) all my life because my family does well with laid-back cats and we have a small home. I've also rescued cats and those are much more of a crap shoot for personality. Doesn't mean I loved them any less, but there were issues with jumping on counters, scratching furniture and needed activity level that I've never had with a [fluffy breed].

That said, it's entirely possible to find rescue purebred cats, as it is dogs, if you look around and are willing to wait.

Pointe shoes haven't changed in hundreds of years, not that someone doesn't come along now and then and suggest that improvements could and should be made. But the ballet world is steeped in tradition and doesn't change quickly. How banged up your feet get is really depends on how often you dance and how frequently you are on pointe. It's the professionals top-tier dancers who end up with feet like this.

Source: 13 years of ballet. Knees and ankles completely fucked. Feet OK because I wasn't on pointe much and wasn't a professional.
AS IS TRADITION, YOU WERE REPORTED.
It's made me nervous for ages.
Knees and ankles for me. My ankles were the first to go.

>this is totally normal?

It's only normal for professional dancers who are on pointe a lot. The average girl dancing for fun in a local school/production does not experience this particular problem, but ballet as a whole puts a huge strain on the female body and the culture can be quite unhealthy at competitive levels. Eating disorders and drug abuse are extremely common and there is an insane amount of pressure to look a "certain" way with regard to body size and shape (and ethnicity if we're being honest). There has been progress on some fronts in the past few decades, but it's slow going. Suggest reading Gelsey Kirkland's "Dancing on my Grave" if you're interested.

TL;DR - your kid dancing in the holiday production of Nutcracker doesn't have these feet, but ballet at the highest levels can be really toxic.
